headline: CRUDE DROPS 3.5% AS GRAINS GRIND HIGHER ON NO NEWS
lead: Corn held $5.00 flat, beans ticked up to $12.77, and crude fell 3.5% to $89.37 on Gulf export flow that's actually working this time. That's the real story today: oil giving back the fear premium while grains just sit there, unbothered.
teaser: Crude drops 3.5% on Gulf flows while corn and beans barely blink at $5.00 and $12.77.

one_number.unit: per head loss on fed cattle
one_number.context: Farm Bureau says ranchers are eating losses up to $400 a head on rising beef imports while retail prices dropped just 16 cents since Labor Day.

yesterdays_call.note: Corn never got near $5.09; it sat flat at $5.00 all session, the breakout thesis stalled cold.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called corn up toward $5.09 ($5.0375 when the call was made). It closed at $5.0.

action: Crude under $89.37 and falling: lock any diesel needs now, this Gulf-flow story isn't done unwinding.

sections.title: Crude Gives Back More Ground
sections.body:
- WTI fell 3.5% to **$89.37**, the second straight session lower as Gulf export flows rebound and take the fear premium out of the barrel.
- Oilprice.com reports Brent holding above $102 even as U.S. troop movements continue, the rebound in Persian Gulf flows is simply outweighing the headlines.
sections.so_what: Gulf flows are breaking the fear premium faster than geopolitics can rebuild it.

sections.title: Grains Sit On Their Hands
sections.body:
- Corn closed flat at **$5.00**, beans added a penny to $12.77, wheat was the mover at $6.86, up 1%.
- Feedstuffs called Thursday's bean cuts 'moderate'; today's bounce looks like position-squaring, not new demand.
- World Grain flagged winter crop dryness easing, which takes a little weather premium out of the wheat board even as it firms.
sections.so_what: No fresh catalyst; the board is waiting on the next data point, not trading one.

sections.title: Cattle Firm, Cull Cows Don't
sections.body:
- Live cattle ticked up to **$219.35**, feeders ran 0.8% higher to $339.30, but the cull cow market is the one actually breaking down.
- Beef Magazine reports cull cow values falling sharply on rising slaughter and drought-driven liquidation, a different animal than the fed cattle trade.
sections.so_what: Fed cattle strength is masking real stress lower in the cow herd.

outside_the_pit.title: Farmers Push Back On Rising Beef Imports
outside_the_pit.body: Farm Bureau data shows ranchers losing up to $400 a head while grocery prices barely moved, a gap that's becoming a policy fight.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above 50% keeps basis at seasonal lows, below 35% firms it fast.
Export sales; beans above 1.5MMT keeps $12.77 as support, below 1MMT tests the range lower.
WTI below $87.50 next session confirms the Gulf-flow unwind is real, not a one-day fade.

daily_quote.text: It was never my thinking that made the big money for me. It always was my sitting.

source_summary: CME locked price table, feedstuffs.com, world-grain.com, beefmagazine.com, oilprice.com, thefencepost.com, farmdocdaily.illinois.edu
